reason: E1 mentions dynamic oxygen embrittlement in similar alloys and a ductility drop in TiZrHfNbTa at 1073 K, supporting the premise that HfNbTaTiZr is susceptible to oxygen-related degradation. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence on ALD alumina coatings, their barrier properties on refractory HEAs, or their adhesion under the specified conditions, leaving the core intervention premises entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: HfNbTaTiZr suffers from oxygen embrittlement at high temperatures
An ultrathin ALD alumina coating can act as a dense, inert oxygen diffusion barrier
The coating will remain adherent and intact under thermal and mechanical loading at ~1000 °C
Preventing oxygen uptake preserves the alloy's ductility and yield strength
